svg.text: THE FASTENER SANDWICH AT ONE MAGNET
True section through one magnet position, drawn at one scale on both axes - 4.6 px/mm across AND through. One drawing per distinct stack shape.
Plate 4.75 mm (0.187 in), hole O8.5 mm, stud a fixed 12.70 mm (0.500 in). Change any of those and every panel here changes with it.
The orange band is where that part actually touches the plate. Part numbers are McMaster-Carr, read off their tables on 2026-08-27.
Washer thickness is the MAX of the range it is sold to - every stack is checked against the thickest one that might ship.
Showing the 17 stack shapes that fit or are marginal, out of 39 permutations. Threadlocker changes locking, not geometry, so it has no separate panel - see fastener_matrix.svg for all of them.
JAM nut (half height) + OVERSIZED washer O1.250
JAM nut (half height) + flat washer O0.750
THIN nylon-insert locknut + OVERSIZED washer O1.250
THIN nylon-insert locknut + flat washer O0.750
standard hex nut + OVERSIZED washer O1.250
standard hex nut + flat washer O0.750
USE: JAM nut (half height) + OVERSIZED washer O1.250 + threadlocker
4.75 + 1.52 + 4.76 = 11.04 mm against a 12.70 mm stud: +1.66 mm to spare, and 732 mm2 of bearing - the most of any stack that fits, 10x a bare nut.
The half-height JAM nut is what buys the room: it is 1.59 mm shorter than the thinnest LOCKNUT, which is exactly what a washer costs. Locking is chemical instead - threadlocker adds no height at all.

Runner-up is the THIN nylon-insert locknut, no washer: 11.10 mm used, +1.60 mm spare, and a MECHANICAL lock that needs no chemical and survives being taken apart. It bears on only 70 mm2 - which is harmless, so this is a preference, not a correctness call.
Fasteners are BLACK OXIDE where stocked - only the ARM nuts are visible, facing up against a textured-black arm.
